page.layout: One page of running text, with two marginal notes in the left margin ("Maior." and "Minor.") beside the paragraphs they introduce. Running head at the top, page number at the top left.

main_text.p: natura Dei summè sapientis, summè boni, summè etiam φιλανθρώπ[?]ης.

Maior. Est hoc Deo solenne, se invocates exaudire, opemq; eius implorantibus succurrere. Juxta dulcissima haec oracula: Oculi Jehouae sunt super justos: & aures eius (intentae) ad clamorem eorum. Vultus autem Jehouae super facientes malu, ut exscindat e terra memoriam eorum. Clamant (afflicti) & Jehouah audit: & ex omnibus angustiis eorum liberat eos. Psal. 34.15.16.17. Item: Erit praeterea, antequam clament, ego audiam: adhuc ipsis loquentibus, ego audiam: Isa.65.24. Huc referri potest universalis experietia omnium Sanctorum, de qua dicitur: In te speraverunt patres nostri: speraverunt, & liberasti eos. Ad te clamaverunt, & liberati sunt: in te speraverunt, & non sunt pudefacti: Psal. 22.4.5. Et illud eiusdem Dauidis dictum[?], experientia comprobatum: Multa sunt adversa justis: sed tamen ex ijs omnibus liberat eos Jehouah. Psal.34.19.
Minor. Ego vero, inquit Habacuc, jam diu multumq; ad Jehouam clamavi, nec tamen mihi videor exauditus: ac manifestam notoriamq; vim passus, pro defen-sione

page.notes: Greek word at the end of the first line is uncertain (φιλανθρώπ...), final letters read with doubt. "dictum" in "Dauidis dictum" is hard to read in the scan (printed as "di ftum" with a space), so it is marked. Running head and page number are clear. The last line of the page "fione" is read as "sione" (defen-sione), the paragraph continues on the next page. Printed spelling "malu", "Pfal." (long s) and "Isa." are kept as printed.
